88632.title: Sales and Advisor Analysis reports drop a voided invoice and keep its re-invoice
88632.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in a fresh test location made for this run, so nothing else is invoiced, credited or clocked there; on the Dashboard, the Revenue tile on This Week reads $0.00 with 0 Invoices.
  3. You run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week.
  4. A test customer with one contact and one asset that uses that contact (for example ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer 1, contact Dana Test, unit ZZ-101).
  5. Technician 1 is you (Admin ShopView, Time Clock on): in a fresh location you are the technician offered in Add Technician, and you clock time yourself.
  6. Advisor A: you (Admin ShopView); the Service Advisor in the work order's left panel shows your name by default.
  7. One invoiced work order (not sent, not paid) for that customer, Service Advisor Advisor A, one labor line: What Are You Doing? ZZAUTOTEST Line 1, Technician 1, $100.00 an hour, Estimated Time 2.00, Tech Time 2.00, with exactly 2.00 hours clocked on it. You have written down its Subtotal (e.g. $200.00).

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: create a fresh location for every run (use a new name each time, for example ZZAUTOTEST Quiet plus today's date and a letter): profile icon > Settings > Locations > New Location: Name, Address 1, City, State/Province, ZIP/Postal Code, Timezone, Telephone, Shop Supplies Charge 0 > Save & Close. Switch to it: click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. While you are in it, add the labor rate this test uses (rates belong to each location): profile icon > Settings > Labor Rates > New Labor Rate: Name (for example ZZAUTOTEST Rate 100, Rate 100) > Save & Close. Check: Dashboard > Revenue tile > range pill > This Week: it reads $0.00 with 0 Invoices.
  • For 4: Customers > New Customer > Name > Save; on its Contacts tab: New Contact; add an asset (Add beside Asset in the New Work Order window, or the customer's Assets tab) and pick that contact in the asset's Contact field.
  • For 5: nothing to set up. To clock time: on the line's Labor row click Start, then Stop > Clock Out (same browser).
  • For 6: the Service Advisor is in the work order's left panel; pick another name there for a second advisor.
  • For 7: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and an Asset (Add beside either if needed) > Save (if a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create); set Service Advisor to Advisor A in the left panel; in the New Line window (> New Line on the Lines tab for each further line): What Are You Doing? ZZAUTOTEST Line 1, Add Technician Technician 1, Labor Rate the $100 rate you added in this location (for example ZZAUTOTEST Rate 100), Estimated Time 2 and Tech Time 2, tick Line Approved > Save & Close; as Technician 1 (yourself): on the line's Labor row click Start, then Stop > Clock Out; as Admin make the clocked time exactly 2.00 hours: three dots at the top right of the Lines tab > Timesheets (1) > edit the record (if it cannot be edited there or in Reports > Timesheet Activities, keep the real time and use the hours Timesheet Activities shows in every sum); on the line click Story (Add tech story for this line) > type a short story > Update; click Complete (if a Missing Details window asks for Mileage, enter one > Complete All Lines); click Mark Reviewed; Finance tab > Create Invoice; close the New Customer Payment window without paying (do not send or pay the invoice). The Subtotal is on the Finance tab.
88632.custom_steps:
1. Click Reports in the top menu, then Sales in the left menu.
  2. Set the Date control to This week.
  3. Write down the row for your invoice and the Subtotal in the Totals row (e.g. $200.00).
  4. Click Advisor Analysis in the left menu (the page is titled Service Advisor Analysis) and set the Date control to This week, with no advisor chosen.
  5. Write down your invoice's row: Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Billing Efficiency, ELR and Subtotal (e.g. 2.00, 2.00, 100.00%, $200.00).
  6. Click Work Orders in the top menu and open the same work order.
  7. On the Lines tab click New Line: What Are You Doing? "ZZAUTOTEST Line 2", Add Technician = Technician 1, Labor Rate = the $100 rate you added in this location (for example ZZAUTOTEST Rate 100), Estimated Time 1.00, Tech Time 1.00, tick Line Approved > Save & Close. (Adding a line while the invoice is still unpaid and unsent voids that invoice.)
  8. On the new line click Story > type a short story > Update, then click Complete (if a window offers Complete All Lines or asks for Mileage, finish it there), then click Mark Reviewed.
  9. Click the Finance tab and write down what it shows for the first invoice (for example a Void label).
  10. Click Create Invoice, close the New Customer Payment dialog without paying, and write down the new Subtotal (e.g. $300.00 = $200.00 + 1.00 hour x $100.00).
  11. Open Reports > Sales again (Date: This week) and write down the rows and the Totals row Subtotal.
  12. Open Reports > Advisor Analysis again (Date: This week, no advisor chosen) and write down the rows and the Totals row.
  13. Try to make an invoice with no customer: Parts > Part Sales > New Part Sale, and see whether the sale can be invoiced without choosing a customer. If the screen insists on a customer, stop this step.
  14. Open the release notes published with this release and look for the note about the Sales and Service Advisor Analysis corrections. The sources do not say where release notes are published: if you cannot find them, write "release note not found" in the result comment and mark only this check Blocked.
88632.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Before the void, the Sales report shows your invoice and its Totals row Subtotal reads $200.00, and Advisor Analysis shows Hrs Worked 2.00, Hrs Invoiced 2.00 and Billing Efficiency 100.00% (2.00 / 2.00 x 100).
  • After the void and re-invoice, the Sales report lists only the new invoice: the voided invoice is gone and the Totals row Subtotal reads $300.00, not $500.00 ($200.00 + $300.00).
  • Advisor Analysis shows one row for the work order, the new invoice, with Hrs Invoiced 3.00 (2.00 + 1.00) and Subtotal $300.00. Hrs Worked stays 2.00, so Billing Efficiency reads 150.00% (3.00 / 2.00 x 100). The figures moved up, which is the void-then-reinvoice case.
  • If you could invoice a sale with no customer, it appears in the Sales report total and in Advisor Analysis. If you could not, write "no-customer invoice not reachable by hand" in the result comment.
  • The release notes carry one plain-language note naming both corrections, and it mentions that a voided-then-reinvoiced figure can move up. This is a check of the published notes, not of the product screens.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S3, context notes under S3-E2. Also the Dashboard v1 Technical Implementation Plan (2026-09-16), NFR-010 and section 7 (how a void is produced), read in full 7 Oct 2026; it informs and never overrules the PRD.

  • S3-E2 context note (Sales report): “That is a defect in the Sales report rather than a dashboard decision, and it is corrected inside this project so Revenue can match it (@chris ruling, 2026-09-15). Correcting it moves the Sales report's own existing totals for any range containing voided or no-company invoices, so it ships with a release note.”
  • S3-E2 context note (Service Advisor Analysis): “That moves advisor revenue and ELR down for periods containing voided invoices and adds walk-in sales to advisor figures, under the same release note.”
